lines.japanese: 話を終えたあと、山科さんは座布団と、それを弄る自分の手を見つめていた。
lines.english: When my story ended, Yamashina gazed at the cushion and at her own hands worrying its fabric.

lines.japanese: 「解離性障害の一つかなあ、でもやっぱり私じゃ判断できないしなあ……いつかちゃんとお医者さんに連れていかないと駄目かな」
lines.english: “Could it be some form of dissociative disorder? But I still can’t judge that myself... I may have to take him to a proper doctor someday.”

lines.japanese: 「でも今それを突きつけても逃げちゃうだけだし、徐々に調律してくしかないか」
lines.english: “If I confront him with it now, he’ll only run away. I suppose I’ll have to bring him gradually into tune.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、大体分かった」
lines.english: “All right. I think I understand the situation.”

lines.japanese: 「なにが？」
lines.english: “Understand what?”

lines.japanese: 彼女は手の動きを止めると、小さく口端を持ち上げた。
lines.english: Her hands grew still, and one corner of her mouth lifted faintly.

lines.japanese: 「つまりお姫様の偽者を殺しちゃったと思ってたら、それが本物だったんだ？」
lines.english: “So you thought you’d killed a fake princess, but she turned out to be the real one?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……で？」
lines.english: “Hmm... And?”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「それで？　どうするの？」
lines.english: “And then? What will you do?”

lines.japanese: 「どうするって……」
lines.english: “What will I do...?”

lines.japanese: それをいま悩んでるんだけど……やっぱり、事の重大さが上手く伝わらなかったのかな。
lines.english: That was precisely what troubled me... Perhaps I had failed to convey the gravity of the matter.

lines.japanese: 「羽田君の世界であることに変わりはないんでしょ。だったら世界を自分で創りかえればいいじゃん」
lines.english: “It’s still your world, isn’t it? Then you can remake it yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、創りかえる？」
lines.english: “What? Remake it?”

lines.japanese: 「もうそっちの世界も楽しいだけじゃないんだよね。だったらこっちの世界に居ても同じことだよ」
lines.english: “That world isn’t all fun anymore either, right? So staying in this one would be no different.”

lines.japanese: 「で、でもそれはおれの意思で選べることじゃないし……」
lines.english: “B-but it isn’t something I can choose for myself...”

lines.japanese: 「だから創りかえればいいと思うよ。そのくらい出来るよ、羽田君はその世界で一番すごいひとなんだから」
lines.english: “That’s why I think you should remake it. You can do that much. You’re the greatest person in that entire world.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、そんな誉められることでもないけどさ」
lines.english: “I-it’s not like I deserve that much praise.”

lines.japanese: 僕が照れたように額を掻くと、山科さんは薄い目をして微笑んでくれた。
lines.english: I scratched my forehead in embarrassment, and Yamashina smiled at me through narrowed eyes.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあいいじゃん。こっちの世界にいつまでも居なよ」
lines.english: “Then it’s settled. Stay in this world forever.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 驚いた。山科さんが渡来さんと同じことを言うなんて思わなかった。
lines.english: I was astonished. I had never expected Yamashina to say the same thing as Watarai.

lines.japanese: 「い、いや、それはその、おれが選べることじゃ……」
lines.english: “N-no, I mean... It isn’t something I can choose...”

lines.japanese: 「試したことあるの？」
lines.english: “Have you ever tried?”

lines.japanese: 「ないよ」
lines.english: “No.”

lines.japanese: 「それ、単に行かなくちゃいけないと思いこんでるだけかもしれないよ」
lines.english: “Then perhaps you’ve only convinced yourself that you have to go.”

lines.japanese: 「だとしてもおれはその……」
lines.english: “Even so, I...”

lines.japanese: 「うん。すぐに答えを出さなくてもいいんじゃないかなあ。どうせまた向こうへ行くなら、そのあとに考えたって」
lines.english: “Mmm. You don’t need an answer right away. If you’re going back there anyway, you can think about it afterward.”

lines.japanese: 「そう……なのかな」
lines.english: “Is that... how it is?”

lines.japanese: 言われてみれば山科さんの言うとおりだ。まだ時間だって少しは残ってるはずだ。
lines.english: Once she said it, I saw that Yamashina was right. I ought to have at least a little time left.

lines.japanese: 僕がこの世界に残してる未練。彼女はそれを望んでくれるんだろうか。
lines.english: The attachment I still had to this world. Was that something she wanted for me?

lines.japanese: 心についた引っかき傷がじわりと疼いた。
lines.english: The scratch upon my heart began slowly to ache.

lines.japanese: 「えっと、山科さんの言うとおり向こうに行ってみないと分からないこともあるし、ちょっと考えてみるよ」
lines.english: “Um... As you say, there are things I can’t know until I return. I’ll give it some thought.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、それでいいと思うよ」
lines.english: “Yes. I think that’s best.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんの笑顔は優しかった。
lines.english: Yamashina’s smile was gentle.

lines.japanese: 「だけどよくおれが考えもしなかったことを思いついたね」
lines.english: “Still, I’m surprised you thought of something that never even occurred to me.”

lines.japanese: 「もともと矛盾だらけだもん」
lines.english: “Because it was full of contradictions from the beginning.”

lines.japanese: 「矛盾？　それはなにが？」
lines.english: “Contradictions? What was?”

lines.japanese: 「私たちの理想像」
lines.english: “The ideal selves we imagine.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、理想？　自分に？　そんなの持ってるつもりはないんだけどなあ」
lines.english: “What? An ideal for myself? I don’t think I have one.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふっ、理想くらいは持っておいた方がいいよ」
lines.english: “Hee hee. You should at least have an ideal to aim for.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、そうだね、こうなればいいな……くらいの期待はあるよ」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes, I suppose I do have hopes for what I might become.”

lines.japanese: 「そうなんだ。私に出来ることがあれば、相談に乗るよ」
lines.english: “I see. If there’s anything I can do, you can always come and talk to me.”

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、山科さん」
lines.english: “Thank you, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「ううん、気にしなくていいよ。心理療法にもならない、ただ話を聞かせてもらったってだけだもん」
lines.english: “There’s no need to thank me. It wasn’t even psychotherapy. I merely listened to you talk.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは座布団を脇に置いた。その代わりに脱いだ上着を引きよせる。
lines.english: Yamashina set the cushion aside and drew her discarded coat toward her in its place.

lines.japanese: どうやら帰る準備みたいだ。遅くまで話を聞いてもらって、助かったな。
lines.english: Apparently she meant to leave. Her willingness to listen so late had been a great help.

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、そろそろ帰るね。羽田君も落ちついたみたいだし」
lines.english: “I should be going. You seem calmer now.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、もう大丈夫だと思う。だけど、どうしておれの相談になんて乗ってくれたの？」
lines.english: “Yes. I think I’m all right. But why did you agree to listen to my troubles?”

lines.japanese: 「ん？　んー……そうだな」
lines.english: “Hm? Mmm... Let me think.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは袖を通しながら、天井を見て考えはじめた。
lines.english: As she put her arms through her sleeves, Yamashina looked at the ceiling and considered.

lines.japanese: 「私の詞に返事をくれたからかな」
lines.english: “Perhaps because you answered my lyrics.”
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: もしかして、この間のお礼ってことか。
lines.english: Could this have been her way of thanking me for the other day?

lines.japanese: 「ありがとう、山科さん」
lines.english: “Thank you, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、さっきも聞いたよ」
lines.english: “Hee hee. You said that already.”

lines.japanese: 山科さんは僕のパソコンに小さくなにか呟くと、襖の方に体を向けて立ちあがる。
lines.english: Yamashina murmured something softly to my computer, then turned toward the sliding door and rose.

lines.japanese: 「あとは、まあー……」
lines.english: “And then, well...”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 襖に手をかけたとき、彼女はもう一度天井を見上げた。
lines.english: With her hand on the door, she looked up at the ceiling once more.

lines.japanese: 「空いてるなら、もらっちゃおうかなあ……」
lines.english: “If no one’s claimed it, maybe I will...”

lines.japanese: 「え、なにを？」
lines.english: “What? Take what?”

lines.japanese: 「あのね、羽田君にはずっと純粋なままでいて欲しいな」
lines.english: “You know, Haneda, I hope you’ll always remain innocent.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　おれって純粋？　なの？」
lines.english: “What? Am I innocent?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、比較的」
lines.english: “Relatively.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、山科さんの期待に応えられるかは分からないけど、頑張ってみるよ」
lines.english: “Mmm. I don’t know whether I can live up to your expectations, but I’ll try.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、期待に応えたら修羅場になるかも」
lines.english: “Mmm. If you do live up to them, it might turn into a bloodbath.”

lines.japanese: 「なにそれ。あ、あとさっきの、空いてたらもらうってどういうこと？」
lines.english: “What does that mean? And what did you mean before, about taking something if it was unclaimed?”

lines.japanese: 「なんだろうね。じゃあ、バイバイ」
lines.english: “Who knows? Well, bye-bye.”

lines.japanese: 僕の質問には答えないまま、右手をぱくぱくさせて出ていった。
lines.english: Without answering, she opened and closed her right hand in farewell and left.

lines.japanese: 一瞬ぽかんとしてしまったけど、慌ててあとを追い、外まで見送る。
lines.english: For an instant I stood blankly. Then I hurried after her and saw her off outside.

lines.japanese: 本当にありがとう、山科さん。もし今日、君に会えなかったら、僕にはもう行き場がなかったかもしれない。
lines.english: Thank you, truly, Yamashina. Had I not met you today, perhaps there would have been nowhere left for me to go.

lines.japanese: 長い一日でどっと疲れが出たけど、まだ頭は冴えている。さあ、文集制作に取りかかろう。
lines.english: The long day had exhausted me all at once, yet my mind remained sharp. Very well. Time to begin work on the graduation anthology.
